body:
I bought four hits of acid that had apparently been double-dipped from a friend of a friend of a friend about a week ago. My knowledge of those four hits in my freezer started to make me anxious. I didn't know if I should dose, I didn't feel ready. I didn't want to re-sell them because all my friends are more experienced in hallucinogens than I am and I would have had to sell them for a few dollars less than I bought them for. Anyway, I'd given my friend 30$ to buy these four hits, and then I'd had to leave her house so I couldn't be there to buy them. I guessed she'd gotten two hits for me (because she told me they were four hits and to just cut each one in half, but I didn't believe her) and tricked me. So I asked her to be honest if she had, and she said she hadn't, and I believe her because I trust her quite a bit.  A night before my actual trip, I took a little less than a quarter of a tab (hardly anything) and smoked some really great weed, alone, before I went to bed, just to get a teeny bit of a feel for it. The quarter tab just heightened and strengthened my weed high for about three hours longer than I'd have expected, and the weed eased me into being able to sleep. I woke up feeling fine, well-rested, and assured that acid is a good drug.
The day after taking the quarter tab, I went to dinner with my parents and sister at this really cool brazilian restaurant. I planned to take the rest of the the tab that night as soon as my family were all in their rooms on their way to a night full of sleep.
I did this acid alone
. I have severe social anxiety, and acid heightens each sense I have, so I feared having a freakout with people because I was already predisposed to it just being sober. So I chose to do it alone.
I took half of the tab at 10:20 p.m. and figured it would kick in at 11:00. I told myself that if I didn't feel anything at  11:00, I would just take the rest of the tab. That's what ended up happening. I laid in bed while the rest of the tab dissolved, which ended up taking about 15 minutes because my sense of time was already distorted since the acid half-tab from earlier had actually kicked in.  I got up and went to my computer, to read up about acid even more than I already had (I had read about it alot at this point). Quickly I started to feel this warm dissociative rush of euphoria and a logical derangement of my senses. This was a really great part. For me, it felt almost like someone I really liked was approaching me from behind to hug me. A sort of pleasure-anxiety. This lasted for at least an hour straight. I also felt kind of weak, too - lightheaded, like the first time you chain smoke cigarettes when you're a kid and get a really intense head high. Dazed. Soon it was 12:30, and this euphoric thing was still going on. Suddenly, I was so tuned in to the world around me it was unbelievable. It was this wonderful joy of simply existing. I really felt this radiance of just being there. Each breath I took was a lifetime in itself. Suddenly, after maybe forty minutes of this, the visuals started.
About an hour and ten minutes after I started feeling the effects of the acid (they had started at about 11:45), I had turned the webcam on my computer on, to tape my tripping and watch it when I was sober and laugh at things I'd said or done. When the visual effects of my trip set in, I began to stare at myself in the webcam. My face would distort. Each movement I'd make - if my lips turned up in a smile it would be exaggerated and my lips would be dragged and hook to my pupils in a frightening chelsea-grin kind of situation, if my eyes would widen (since I wanted to see everything) my eyes would grow immensely and I'd look like a cartoon. If I rolled my head back or moved it at all really, my face would seem to melt. I began to wonder if it was just my webcam, because although it was amusing it was also mildly terrifying. I looked across the room, everything looked basically normal. Then I looked at the surface of my desk and my bulletin board, and the desk surface rippled and moved like an ocean and the bulletin board was an entire world within itself. It was astounding, but not as impressive as the facial distortions.
Then I turned and looked into the mirror that's right by my desk. My face distorted in the same ways, but it was scarier because it was really me, it wasn't just 'the girl in the webcam' which was how I had been viewing myself. I got up to go to the bathroom and drink some water from the sink and try to sober up a little bit, because I knew I had just fallen into the acid trip. Something in my brain had been turned on. As I walked to the bathroom, I felt disconnected from my body. I didn't feel like I was walking. 'Who's walking?' I asked myself out loud. Speaking was even more shocking than moving. In my head I thought, 'Is that me speaking, or someone else? I know it's me but I just can't connect that voice to me.' I went to the bathroom, tried to relax. Two or three minutes passed, which felt like three days. I walked back out of the bathroom, after a half hour more of staring at myself in the mirror, the facial distortions even more intense - my face would appear as dozens of other faces
my face would appear as dozens of other faces
- some skeletal, some demonic, some childish, some feminine, some masculine, some black, some white, and this is when the physical 'I' began to fade from my perception. That was terrifying. I couldn't talk. I couldn't look at myself. I would touch my face and not believe that it was the same face reflected in the mirrors. It was impossible to tell myself, either out loud or in my head that 'Come on, you'll be okay' or even 'I'm okay, I'm okay, I'm alright, I'm just on acid' because 'I' and 'me' and 'my' and 'Self' became complete illusions.
Suddenly, I had a moment of insight so profound that I shocked myself. I realized that the illusion of Ego is so unrelated to anything physical that self-hate and self-consciousness is a waste of time. Each aspect of my personality and my body that I had been taught was improper or otherwise began to dissolve, and then my true self was just there, existing, breathing in, letting go, and I calmed down almost completely. At that point in my head I laughed and I thought, 'Fuck this, I'm a teenager, I just want to have fun.' So I put on some stereotypical acid-trip music (Hendrix, Beatles, etc.) and watched my ceiling transform into psychedelic rainbow mayan hieroglyphs or ancient texts or impressionist paintings, lit some candles and watched the light dance, and just flew threw the illusion of time for two or three hours.
And then I got heartburn. And started to freak out again. 'I'm drenched in acid....Acid heartburn....nausea....headache...I'm gonna die, I'm in psychosis' my thoughts started to get the best of me. I went back to my computer for an hour to try to calm down, but I just got on facebook and looked at pictures of my friends. It was strange, my miniature taste of Ego death earlier had also affected my perception of people I knew and would normally judge. But I would just look at these people and see them as human, not as ugly or pretty or fat or skinny or annoying or bland or fun or boring or anything- just as people. I went to the bathroom to try to go pee, but I couldn't, and I stared at myself in the mirror again for about an hour, drank some water, and then decided I really needed to eat something. I had some vegan chocolate and dried mangoes in my room and so I ate some of those, which were both sensational and amazing while I was on acid. Then I listened to some music and tripped out on the objects in my room, but 20 minutes later maybe I started seeing the shadows jump up and hearing noises from my attic fan as my parents were coming upstairs. I went and got my laptop to read about peoples acid experiences so I could relate to someone, and then I felt this crushing loneliness. I wanted to go get my parents and tell them I was tripping and ask if they wanted to trip with me. I felt horrible. I told myself I couldn't let this sadness overtake a drug experience because it is too all-consuming, so I watched some videos of Richard Alpert talking about LSD.
Soon it was 5:30 I had faced the fact I wouldn't sleep. By 5:45, my body was almost reunited with my mind. I no longer felt separated into parts - body, mind, senses, drug, ego - but my vision was still more colorful and layered and artistic. There was this wonderful art in every thing that I saw. I decided to go for a walk, so I pulled on some sweatpants and put on my shoes and went downstairs. My dad was sleeping on our couch, and woke up grumpily, asking me where I was going. It was really sketch, and I still could hardly manage to talk. I went for a walk, then sat and watched the sunrise for an hour and a half.  I was still on acid, and the sunrise was so incredibly beautiful it brought tears to my eyes. The joy of existing from the very beginning of the trip was back, the anxiety was gone. I went back inside (and by now it was almost 8:00am) got my cat to bring upstairs and a nectarine for breakfast, then went back to my room and watched ten minutes of family guy, tried to eat the nectarine (but my appetite was killed by the LSD) and then fell asleep until noon. When I woke up I was really dazed, tired, and really dehydrated, and I felt like two weeks had passed instead of one night.
My perception is still changed, and this was two weeks ago. Everything is art. Everything is a little better. Everything is a little more beautiful. I will DEFINITELY do acid again, but probably in the fall because I can't stand heat and comfortable weather always makes for a better trip.
